title: Streaming metering flush duplicates on reconnect leading to transient double-billing
creator: Liam Chen
description: Summary: When a long-lived streaming generation is interrupted and the client reconnects using an ephemeral stream identifier that collides with the previous stream, the streaming aggregator can emit both the original flush and the reconnect flush. This results in duplicate token/usage debits for the same logical content. Impact surface: hosted API streaming, Dedicated streaming edge, and Private ingest adapters that use the same summarizer + flush path. Occurs only when: (a) the client reconnects within the dedup window, and (b) the ephemeral stream id is reused (client or proxy bug), and (c) the final flush from the prior connection is still in-flight or retried at the aggregator layer.
repro_steps: 1) Start a long-running streaming generation (client A) that produces a few hundred tokens over ~30s
2) Interrupt the connection (TCP reset or client close) right before the normal 'stream_close' flush triggers
3) Reconnect immediately from a new client instance (client B) that — due to a buggy proxy/SDK path — reuses the same ephemeral stream_id string

4) The streaming summarizer receives the original flush (delayed) and the new connection's partial state; both paths trigger a flush/finalize which are each converted into a usage debit event and emitted to the metering pipeline
5) Observe two debit events for the same logical generation in the billing stream / usage dashboards and an immediate transient throttle for that credential if quota was tight
observed_logs_and_signals: aggregator:stream_flush: emitted flush_id=abc123 stream_id=sid-7f9 delay_ms=3200 status=retry
ingest:meter-emitter: debit_event id=debit-987 stream_id=sid-7f9 tokens=342 credential=cred-42
ingest:meter-emitter: debit_event id=debit-988 stream_id=sid-7f9 tokens=342 credential=cred-42
client-proxy: reused ephemeral id due to local cache bug (repro in SDK v0.17.2)
root_cause: The streaming aggregator's flush path assumes stream_id is unique and uses it as the primary de-duplication key. Because ephemeral stream IDs can be (incorrectly) reused by upstream clients/proxies, and because the aggregator's idempotency window is centered only on flush_id and not combined with generation UUIDs, duplicate flushes within the idempotency window are accepted and converted into separate debit events. Additionally, the emitter's retry handling (at-least-once) can re-emit a flush that overlaps with a fresh flush from a reconnect when the stream_id collides.
impact_estimate: ~0.03% of streaming sessions based on sampling from 2026-02-24 to 2026-02-26; approximately 1.2% of affected credentials saw transient quota spikes leading to throttles. Potential revenue variance (overcount) estimated at $1.1k/month at current usage levels if left unmitigated.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Hotfix: Ignore incoming flushes where flush_id already seen within 10s for the same credential + generation fingerprint (de-dup by (credential, generation_checksum) instead of stream_id alone)
2) Deploy a filter in metering-emitter to collapse identical debit events within a 30s window for the same credential and token count (protects against double-emits during rollouts)
3) Notify SO/SE teams and include a guidance blurb for SDKs to avoid reusing ephemeral stream IDs (workaround)
4) Create automated alert: >1 duplicate debits per minute per 10k streaming sessions
long_term_fix_plan: 1) Change aggregator semantics: attach a stable generation UUID at stream start (server-assigned) and require flush de-dup against (credential, generation_uuid, flush_seq)
2) Update SDK/proxy guidance and add defensive server-side validation rejecting reused client-provided ephemeral IDs
3) Add end-to-end property tests in integration harness with simulated reconnects and flaky networks to prevent regressions

4) Add a reconciliation job that scans for pairs of very-similar debit events (same credential, same token count, same generation checksum within 60s) and flags them for billing adjustment / manual review
5) Backfill corrections for affected customers (billing adjustments) and produce a public postmortem if customer-visible billing discrepancies are >$5k
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: - Short term dedupe in emitter reduces some duplicates but can mask real rapid successive independent flushes; we use token_count + checksum heuristics to mitigate false-positives
- Server-assigned generation UUID adds a round trip for some clients; we can assign lazily on first token to minimize latency overhead
- Strict rejection of reused ephemeral IDs will break buggy clients but prevents silent overcharging; we'll swing this behind an opt-in flag for Private customers during rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for generation UUID assignment and flush de-dup logic
Integration test simulating reconnect with reused stream_id and asserting single debit emitted
Load test to ensure emitter collapse filter doesn't create latency regressions under 95th percentile throughput
Canary rollout monitoring with attribution metrics and false-positive rate tracking
rollout_plan: 1) Merge aggregator PR behind feature flag, run integration tests
2) Canary deploy to <10% of streaming traffic (region=eu-west-1) with real-time duplicate metrics monitored
3) If canary stable for 24h, increase to 50% and run reconciliation scan, then to 100%
4) Deploy emitter collapse filter globally after aggregator fix is validated
5) Run billing backfill script for 3-day window and reach out to affected customers
